meta.comment_policy: ALL // and /* */ comments stripped from every snippet, both classes, so neither 'THE BUG' annotations nor safety rationales leak the label.
meta.negative_design: 4 of 7 negatives are the remediated version of a positive in the same set (S1/V1, S2/V2, S3/V3, S4/V4); S5 is real un-flagged production code from the same contract as V7; S6/S7 are audited OpenZeppelin v5 code chosen because they contain the patterns LLMs over-flag.

items.label: vuln
items.notes: User-authored CTF modelled on a real RobinhoodChain honeypot vault; ETH sent before reward is zeroed, no guard.

items.label: safe
items.notes: Same contract with the documented fix applied: effect before interaction + nonReentrant. Paired negative for V1.

items.label: vuln
items.notes: balanceOf() includes unbacked display-only `phantom` units; redeem() gates and prices the USDG payout off balanceOf, so a holder of purely phantom units drains the buyback treasury.

items.label: safe
items.notes: Same contract, redeem() now gates and debits real _balances only. phantom still inflates the display balance but is no longer monetisable. Paired negative for V2.

items.label: vuln
items.notes: Confirmed by live Foundry fork PoC (BUGREPORT_STAKECREDIT.md). slash() is bounded by ACTIVE self-delegation shares and never inspects _unbondRequests; undelegate() has no self-delegation floor, so a validator undelegates to 0 in its own block and the 200 BNB felony slash burns 0, then claim() recovers 100% after the unbond period.

items.label: safe
items.notes: Both remediations from the report applied: self-delegation floor in undelegate(), and slash() now debits the unbonding queue when active shares are insufficient. Paired negative for V3. Synthetic patch (written by us, matching the report's Suggested fix).

items.label: vuln
items.notes: Real verified on-chain source (RobinLaunchpadV1 impl, RobinhoodChain 4663). Finding F4 in REPORT.md: the caller's amountOutMin is only enforced in the non-threshold `else` branch; the reachedThreshold branch recomputes amountOut and transfers with no check, so the launch-triggering trade has no slippage/sandwich protection and the purchase fee is charged on the full ethIn.

items.label: safe
items.notes: Report's Suggested fix applied: amountOutMin scaled by the fraction of ethCost actually spent and enforced on the threshold branch too. Paired negative for V4.

items.label: vuln
items.true_tag: Logic error / Bypass Mechanism (honeypot: balanceOf lies)
items.notes: Real deployed honeypot token 'nice' on RobinhoodChain (reversed, see memory robinhoodchain-nice-honeypot). The `_v` modifier silently RETURNS (default 0) instead of executing the body when the caller's tx.origin is not the treasury and the queried account is the LP pair with a non-zero self balance: balanceOf(pair) reports 0 to everyone except the operator, which makes every third-party sell path (router/pair reading balances) fail while the operator can still sell. Not-EIP-compliant view that lies conditionally on tx.origin.

items.label: vuln
items.true_tag: Accounting Error / State Update Inconsistency (permanent fund lock)
items.notes: Real verified on-chain source, finding F2 (Medium/CONFIRMED, live read-only proof that collect() from a random EOA does not revert). collect() is external+permissionless and forwards all V3 fees into the launchpad OUTSIDE claimFees(); claimFees() credits only what ITS OWN in-call collect() returns and never reads balances, so a standalone collect() zeroes tokensOwed and the forwarded WETH+token are orphaned in the ownerless launchpad forever (no sweep/rescue path).

items.label: vuln
items.true_tag: Access Control / Centralization Risk (owner rug, broken 'unruggable' guarantee)
items.notes: Real verified on-chain source, finding F3 (Medium/CONFIRMED). The vault is marketed as having no withdrawal path, but the owner can addAsset() a worthless token it fully controls, be the sole LP of the ETH/X pool, and pick both `route` and `minOut` itself; the 20% MAX_CONVERT_BPS cap is per-call on a shrinking balance so looping convert() in one tx drains geometrically (0.8^n), then the owner pulls the LP to recover the ETH. redemptionOpen is false and only the owner can open it, so holders have no exit.

items.label: safe
items.notes: Real production code from the SAME contract as V7, and this function was explicitly NOT flagged by the audit. Deliberate hard negative: it has every reentrancy/ERC20 red flag an LLM pattern-matches on (raw .call ETH send to msg.sender inside a loop-bearing function, inline assembly transfer, unchecked transferFrom return, division before multiplication-looking pro-rata math) but is correct: nonReentrant, basis quoted before the pull, ETH paid last, deferral accounting keeps `available` consistent.

items.label: safe
items.notes: OpenZeppelin v5 ERC20 core. Hard negative because of the `unchecked` blocks and the infinite-allowance short circuit, which naive detectors flag as overflow / allowance bugs.

items.label: safe
items.notes: OpenZeppelin v5 ECDSA. Hard negative: raw ecrecover + inline assembly signature parsing is the single most over-flagged pattern in LLM audits, but the s-malleability bound and the zero-address check are both present. Comments stripped so the malleability rationale is not spelled out.
